use_case: AI alert triage in the website security service (SYS-05): scores each malware and vulnerability finding, writes a short explanation, and auto-dismisses findings it rates as false positives or low risk
vendor_or_model: Website security service vendor feature (machine learning scoring plus a generated plain-language explanation)
data_categories: Site files and file changes on 270 customer sites; scan findings; visitor IP addresses; site user names in findings about new administrator users
affects_individuals: Yes (indirectly: shoppers, tenants, and clients whose data sits on customer sites if a compromise is missed)
consequential_decision_category: Safety/CI (security monitoring of hosting services for about 150 businesses); no decision about any person
human_in_the_loop: None today: auto-dismissed findings are never seen by a person. Conditions add human review before any finding in the protected categories is closed, a weekly review, and a monthly sample of 50
applicable_laws: FTC Act Sec. 5 (15 U.S.C. 45(a): website claim "Enterprise-grade malware protection on every site"; 45(n): reasonable security); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) and (6)(a) (a missed compromise delays the 10-day customer notice); vendor terms (data use and location unverified); no sector AI rule identified
status: In production since 2026-05-04; approved with conditions 2026-09-28

use_case: Consumer generative AI chat assistant used by the owner to analyze server log excerpts and suspicious files
vendor_or_model: Consumer chat assistant, free personal account (vendor-hosted large language model)
data_categories: Pasted log excerpts with shopper emails and IP addresses; site files; one configuration file with a database password
human_in_the_loop: Owner reads every answer; no review of what is pasted
applicable_laws: FTC Act Sec. 5 (Terms of Service confidentiality promise; reasonable security); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2); consumer terms allow use of inputs to improve the service
status: Prohibited for customer data, logs, site files, and credentials (POL-01 9.4, adopted 2026-09-28); exposed database password rotation due 2026-09-30 (P01 R-011); a business-tier tool with no-training terms may be assessed later
